tuples.evidence: `claude-opus-5` is the full name of the top-tier model, and the row names it rather than the `opus` alias on purpose: an alias names whatever the vendor points it at today, and a rating keyed on one keeps its evidence and its assessedAt through a re-point (PB-13.1). The name is one the binary takes, and that was run rather than inferred: `claude -p --model claude-opus-5 --max-turns 1 'reply with the single word ok'` answered `ok` on 2.1.251 (2026-09-05), so the id is accepted verbatim at lift. `--model`'s own help says it takes an alias or a model's full name, and the installed binary carries the model table those names come from — the id sits there next to family `opus`, found by grepping the binary, which is the only model listing this harness publishes at all: no `models` subcommand and no `--list-models`. The driver reports the same id as its inventory (MODEL_IDS, lib/driver-claude.js). `max` is the deepest level `claude --effort` names, so it buys the most reasoning and costs the most time and plan. The reviewer quotaCost override is one point lower because a review turn reads a diff and writes notes rather than driving a whole task.

Same model as claude-opus-max — the pinned id `claude-opus-5`, not the `opus` alias — one level down the `claude --effort` ladder: the level below `max` keeps the top tier's quality on ordinary work and gives back some time and plan.

The middle of the effort ladder `claude --effort` publishes in its own help (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) on the top-tier model `claude-opus-5`: the level's own meaning is the whole claim here. The driver knows a sixth level, `ultracode` (lib/driver-claude.js EFFORT_LEVELS), and no tuple rates it: it is xhigh plus dynamic workflow orchestration rather than a point on this ladder, it is gated on a binary version, and there is no source for what it costs against the plan.

Top-tier model `claude-opus-5` at a level below the middle of the `claude --effort` ladder. Worker only by decision, not by rating: claude-opus-high is the lowest level the maintainers will put a review on, because a review that reasons less than the work it reviews finds less than it costs.

`claude-sonnet-5` is the full name of the mid tier, below `claude-opus-5`, and the row names the id rather than the `sonnet` alias for the reason claude-opus-max states. Run rather than inferred, the same way: `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5 --max-turns 1 'reply with the single word ok'` answered `ok` on 2.1.251 (2026-09-05). The binary carries the id in the same model table, next to family `sonnet`, and the driver reports it as its inventory. `high` is the middle of the `claude --effort` ladder.
The cheapest rated Claude tuple: the mid-tier model `claude-sonnet-5` at a level below the middle of the `claude --effort` ladder. This is the row an `economy` run is meant to reach on this harness.

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `claude-opus-5-thinking-max` verbatim, under the display name "Claude Opus 5 1M Max Thinking" (listing captured in test/fixtures/model-catalog/cursor-models.txt). Read the id, not the display name: Cursor's display names drop the level word the id carries, so the `model` field is the id exactly as listed. Top tier of its family, thinking mode, `max` — the deepest and slowest level Cursor exposes for it. `effort` is null because Cursor takes the level inside the model id, never as a flag (lib/driver-cursor.js).

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `claude-opus-5-thinking-high` verbatim, under the display name "Claude Opus 5 1M Thinking" — the display name has no level word, the id does, and the id is what `--model` takes. Same family and mode as cursor-opus-5-thinking-max, one level down.

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `claude-opus-5-high` verbatim, under the display name "Claude Opus 5 1M". It is cursor-opus-5-thinking-high without the thinking segment, so it answers faster and reasons less deeply on the same top-tier model.

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `claude-sonnet-5-thinking-high` verbatim, under the display name "Claude Sonnet 5 1M Thinking": mid tier of the same family as the Opus rows above, in thinking mode.

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `gpt-5.6-sol-high` verbatim, under the display name "GPT-5.6 Sol 1M High". It is the same model Codex's own `model/list` describes as a "Reliable agentic workhorse for everyday tasks", reached through a second harness — which is what makes it useful for reviewer diversity.

`cursor-agent models` lists the id `composer-2.5` verbatim, under the display name "Composer 2.5", with no level suffix at all — so there is no deeper level of it to rate. Cursor's own model and the driver's DEFAULT_MODEL (lib/driver-cursor.js), which records that most of the Cursor spike was measured on it.

`model/list` over `codex app-server` returns gpt-5.6-sol with isDefault true, description 'Reliable agentic workhorse for everyday tasks', and `max` among its supportedReasoningEfforts described as 'Maximum reasoning depth for the hardest problems'. It is also the driver's DEFAULT_MODEL (lib/driver-codex.js).
`model/list` describes gpt-5.6-sol's `xhigh` as 'Extra high reasoning depth for complex problems' — one step below `max`, which is where the time and plan are given back.
`model/list` describes gpt-5.6-sol's `high` as 'Greater reasoning depth for complex problems'.

`model/list` describes gpt-5.6-terra as a 'Balanced agentic coding model for everyday work' with defaultReasoningEffort medium, and its `high` as 'Greater reasoning depth for complex problems'. A second model on the same harness: it gives the reviewer somewhere to go when the worker took gpt-5.6-sol.
`model/list` describes gpt-5.6-sol's `medium` as 'Balances speed and reasoning depth for everyday tasks'.
`model/list` describes gpt-5.6-luna as a 'Fast and affordable agentic coding model' with defaultReasoningEffort medium — the harness's own words for speed and low spend.

`model/list` describes gpt-5.4-mini as 'Small, fast, and cost-efficient model for simpler coding tasks' — the only entry whose own description names a narrower class of task, which is what the quality 2 records.
